issues.title: A duplicate-uuid store row is still reported as `bad_manifest` — the exact mis-attribution this change eliminates elsewhere
issues.description:
The `select(...)` call stays inside the manifest-attributable `try`, so every `CorpusBuildError` it raises becomes `bad_manifest: cannot re-derive from the recorded criteria`. But that clause covers two different culprits. An unsatisfiable recorded `n` genuinely is a manifest defect (correctly pinned by `test_an_unsatisfiable_recorded_n_is_still_a_bad_manifest`). `_group_by_cell`'s `duplicate episode uuid in population` is not — it is unambiguously a STORE condition, and unlike a bad `created_at` it is NOT pre-validated by `fetch_population` (which checks column count, `stratum_key`, and content type, but never uuid uniqueness), so it is reachable from the CLI on a live graph.

Verified by running it against a synthetic population with one duplicated record:

    duplicate-uuid population -> bad_manifest | cannot re-derive from the recorded criteria: duplicate episode uuid in population: '00000124-...' — dispos...

An operator gets exit 5, whose documented remedy is "the artifact is structurally unusable" / "re-derive, or investigate tampering", and goes off to rebuild a corpus that is perfectly correct while the duplicated node in FalkorDB stays put. That is the same wrong-culprit steer the new `_window_population` docstring describes at length.

This matters more than a pre-existing wart because the diff adds a docstring stating the rule as an invariant — `verify_manifest`'s new paragraph says "**Manifest defects are returned; store defects are raised.** ... anything wrong with the population propagates as a CorpusBuildError" — and the duplicate-uuid path makes that statement false as written.

Suggested fix: pull the population-integrity check out the same way the windowing was pulled out (e.g. have `_window_population`, or a sibling helper called alongside it, reject duplicate uuids and raise), leaving only the genuinely criteria-attributable `allocate` failures inside the `try`. The existing control test for unsatisfiable `n` already guards against over-narrowing.
issues.failure_scenario: A `dark_factory` graph that holds two `Episodic` nodes with the same uuid. `--verify` exits 5 (`bad_manifest`) with detail `cannot re-derive from the recorded criteria: duplicate episode uuid in population: '<uuid>'`, so CI and the operator both conclude the committed manifest is broken and re-derive it, while the duplicated store row — the actual defect — is never treated as a store problem. Confirmed by direct execution, not inferred.

issues.title: The new exit-1 cause (`cannot write <--out>`) is missing from both exit-1 cause lists
issues.description:
The module docstring (lines 117-120) glosses exit 1 as "the store was unreachable, or the requested corpus is unsatisfiable", and `scripts/local_memory_models_eval/README.md:54` repeats it as `the run never reached a verdict (store unreachable, unsatisfiable --n)`. The diff adds a third cause — an unwritable `--out`, now raised as `CorpusBuildError(f'cannot write {args.out}: {exc}')` — and neither list was updated.

The exit *code* is unchanged (a raw `OSError` traceback also exited 1), so nothing breaks. But the diff's own test class cites those two documents as the contract it is making true (`TestAnUnreachableStoreIsATypedErrorNotATraceback`'s docstring: "The module docstring's exit table and scripts/local_memory_models_eval/README.md both promise..."), and the whole change is about not sending an operator after the wrong culprit. An operator who hits `error: cannot write ...` and checks the documented cause list finds only "store unreachable" and "unsatisfiable --n" — a list that steers them back toward FalkorDB, which is precisely what `TestAWriteFailureIsNotBlamedOnTheStore` exists to prevent. Add the write-failure case (and, if the finding above is addressed, the corrupt-store-row case) to both lists.
issues.failure_scenario: Operator typos `--out` into a non-directory path, gets `error: cannot write /tmp/afile/corpus_manifest.json: ...` and exit 1, then reads the README's exit-1 row — `(store unreachable, unsatisfiable --n)` — and starts checking FalkorDB connectivity, the exact detour the diff's tests are written to prevent.

issues.title: `test_the_public_wrapper_still_takes_a_raw_population` restates the implementation it checks
issues.description:
The assertion is

    _mod.cell_permutation(pop, cell, seed='s') == _mod._permutation_from_cells(_mod._group_by_cell(pop), cell, seed='s')

and `cell_permutation`'s entire body is `return _permutation_from_cells(_group_by_cell(population), cell, seed=seed)`. So the right-hand side is the left-hand side inlined: the equality holds by construction and cannot detect a behaviour change in either helper — if `_permutation_from_cells` started returning the wrong permutation, both sides move together and the test stays green. (`TestSelect::test_selection_is_a_prefix_of_each_cells_permutation` is what actually pins the permutation's content.)

The residual value is real but narrower than the docstring claims: it pins that `cell_permutation` still accepts an *ungrouped* population, i.e. that the seam was not collapsed into the grouped-only helper. That would be expressed more honestly by dropping the tautological right-hand side and asserting the property the wrapper is there to expose — e.g. that `cell_permutation(pop, cell, seed=...)` returns a permutation of exactly that cell's uuids — which fails if the signature changes AND if the result goes wrong.
issues.failure_scenario: A future refactor breaks `_permutation_from_cells` (say, drops the per-cell RNG derivation so all cells share one stream). This test still passes, because both sides of its equality call the same broken helper — it contributes nothing to catching the regression despite reading as a correctness pin on the seam.

verdict.summary: The change is sound and well-tested. The core idea — attribute a failure at the seam that holds the evidence rather than guessing from `main` — is correctly implemented: `_window_population` is extracted outside the manifest-attributable `try`, the store catch sits in `_fetch_population` (the only place that talks to the store), and the `--out` write guard sits in `_run_build`. `_store_error_types` correctly includes `RedisError`, which is genuinely not an `OSError`, and the handler stays narrow enough that a builder `RuntimeError` still crashes loudly. I verified this by mutation: reverting each of the three production changes independently fails 9 of the new tests, so they pin behaviour rather than restating it. Full file suite: 224 passed; `ruff check` clean on both files. Three findings, none blocking. The substantive one: `verify_manifest` still reports a duplicate-uuid STORE row as `bad_manifest` (exit 5), which is the same mis-attribution class `_window_population` was extracted to eliminate — and the diff's new docstring now states the rule ("Manifest defects are returned; store defects are raised") that this case violates. I confirmed it by running the case directly. The other two are a docs/behaviour drift (the newly-added exit-1 cause is absent from the exit-1 cause lists the diff's own tests cite as the contract) and one test whose equality assertion restates the implementation it checks.
